passage: Note from Divyansh, daycare caregiver. Mohit, two, cried loudly with big tears after lunch. I checked in turn. Hungry? He took a few bites of banana and kept crying. Wet? No. Tired? He rubbed his eyes but pushed away the blanket. Then the vacuum started in the next room, and he flung his arms round my neck. I carried him to the far corner and hummed. He settled in a few minutes.

qa.q: What did Divyansh check first for Mohit's crying?
qa.a: He checked whether Mohit was hungry and offered banana.

qa.q: What does Mohit's grabbing Divyansh when the vacuum started suggest, and what else might have been part of the crying?
qa.a: It suggests fear of the noise as the likely cause. He might also have been tired, since he rubbed his eyes.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do next time?
qa.a: He can check needs one after another, then use quiet closeness before trying to reason.

qa.q: How might Mohit have felt when the first checks did not work?
qa.a: He may have felt more frustrated because his need was still not met.

grounding: A toddler cries loudly with tears, and the caregiver checks needs in turn and soothes before reasoning.

passage: Zubin, two, sat in the doorway of the village house and wailed, tears streaming. His sister Ritu, watching him, ran through what it could be. She offered water and he shoved it away. She felt his clothes; dry. She lifted him and he arched and cried. Then he rubbed his eyes hard, dropped his head on her shoulder and the wail thinned to sniffles. "Sleepy," she said, and rocked him.

qa.q: What did Ritu offer first when Zubin cried?
What does Zubin's rubbing his eyes and dropping his head suggest, and what else could have caused the crying?
qa.a: It suggests tiredness was the main cause. It could also have been frustration or fear before that, since he arched away.

qa.q: What is a good way to respond to a wailing toddler?
qa.a: Check hunger, thirst, comfort and tiredness one after another and soothe him before trying to reason. 🙂

qa.q: How might Zubin have felt while Ritu checked things?
qa.a: He may have felt frustrated that nothing was right yet, then relieved when he was held.

grounding: A toddler cries loudly with tears, and caregivers check needs and offer soothing before reasoning.
